title: Lexington Road cycling path and housing approvals
subtitle: Sugarbush South planning, rental acquisition pilot, Albert Street development, Woolwich Street rezoning, fireworks by-law changes and Hagey Boulevard zoning.
overview: Council accepted the conceptual plan for a multi-use path on the north side of Lexington Road and authorized staff to move to detailed design so the project can meet a federal Active Transportation Fund timeline {{vote:m8}}. The design is meant to narrow the road and improve safety for walking and cycling. Construction is not yet funded.

Council also approved a pilot program to help non-profits buy existing rental buildings {{vote:m9}} and sent draft planning changes for the Sugarbush South neighbourhood out for public consultation {{vote:m7}}. It approved three development applications: 380 Hagey Boulevard {{vote:m11}}, 177-179 Albert Street {{vote:m12}} and 137 and 141 Woolwich Street {{vote:m13}}. Amendments to the Fireworks By-law also passed {{vote:m6}}.

A motion to extend the afternoon session was defeated {{vote:m10}}, so council recessed and resumed at 6:30 p.m. Council met in closed session earlier in the day, and the minutes report no public outcome. The Mayor also noted that the province recognized the city for reaching its 2024 housing target by 129%, with $6.4 million in related funding.

decisions.detail: Council accepted the conceptual plan and authorized staff to progress to detailed design to meet the federal grant timeline, giving consideration to community feedback {{vote:m8}}.
Council approved the pilot program to help non-profits buy existing rental housing and directed staff to develop and publish implementation materials.
Council received the report and directed staff to consult the public and interested parties on the draft Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment and Urban Design Guidelines.
Council approved Official Plan Amendment 52 and Zoning By-law Amendment Z-24-03, changing the affordable housing requirement from 4% of units to 4% of residential density.
Council approved Zoning By-law Amendment Z-24-17 for the lands at 137 and 141 Woolwich Street {{vote:m13}}.
Council approved Zoning By-law Amendment Z-25-07 for 380 Hagey Boulevard.
Council approved report COM2025-021 and amendments to the Fireworks By-law, passed on the consent agenda.

debate: On Lexington Road, a resident delegate said backing out of driveways across a multi-use path would be hard, and raised concerns about emergency vehicles getting through congested traffic, missing street lights on the north side, delivery stops and snow banks. The delegate suggested a south-side path or separate bike lanes on each side.

Staff said the road must be narrowed for traffic calming and that the grant timeline is strict, so reverting to earlier options would put the funding at risk. They said details such as emergency access and lighting could be addressed in detailed design. Councillors differed on whether the motion wording should refer to community feedback, with one saying extensive consultation had already happened.

On Sugarbush South, councillors asked about protection for existing tenants, since the rental replacement by-law is not yet in place. They also asked for high-quality parkettes, attention to extreme heat and tree replacement, accessible street frontages, and a consultation venue closer to the neighbourhood.

On the rental acquisition pilot, councillors asked what safeguards apply if a non-profit defaults, and staff said the grant would be secured on title and could be cancelled. One councillor noted that the six-unit minimum could exclude some smaller lodging houses.

Residents opposing the Albert Street proposal cited height, density, small setbacks, traffic and limited affordable housing. Woolwich Street speakers raised parking, school bus and traffic safety, missing sidewalks, snow storage and privacy.
